title: On‑prem operator upgrade failure: automate rollback and reconcile config drift after customer escalations
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Summary: Several on-prem customer clusters experienced operator crashes and failed Helm upgrades when deploying private/operator v3.2.0 → v3.2.1. Failures manifest as CRD conversion errors (unknown field in v1beta1 -> v1), Helm hooks timing out, and manual node-level edits causing config drift. Customers escalated with degraded control plane and app outages.

Goal: Implement automated safe rollback for failed operator upgrades, ship a targeted hotfix (3.2.1 -> 3.2.1-hotfix1) that tolerates conversion path differences, and add a post-upgrade config reconciliation job to detect and fix drifted values. Provide customer hotfix rollout plan and postmortem.
comments: 2025-02-25 09:12 - Marcus Lee: Incident opened after Customer A reported operator crashloops post-upgrade. Initial triage shows CRD schema mismatch and Helm pre-upgrade hook failed waiting for CRD conversion webhook.
2025-02-25 11:03 - SRE: Reproduced in staging (k8s 1.22). Helm upgrade fails at hook:jobs 'operator-migrate-crds' failed. Operator pod logs show 'unknown field "routingMode" in v1beta1.CRDSpec'.

2025-02-25 14:30 - Ava Chen: Implemented a temporary patch to skip webhook enforcement when converting CRDs; created branch hotfix/skip-webhook-conversion. Need approval from Platform Eng to promote to hotfix release.
2025-02-25 16:50 - PM (Riley Morgan): Escalation call with Customer A/Support scheduled for 2025-02-26 09:00. Communicated that we will schedule a maintenance window and offer a rollback if needed.

2025-02-26 08:40 - Infra (Diego Alves): Observed that 3 of 8 customer clusters had manual overrides in values.yaml (imagePullPolicy, nodeSelector) causing Helm to treat upgrades as no-op for some resources. This is config drift - must reconcile prior to upgrade or include reconciliation step.

2025-02-26 12:15 - Ava Chen: Drafted rollback script (scripts/operator_rollback.sh) that restores last successful Helm release and removes the new CRD webhook temporarily. Smoke-tested rollback in a replica environment; passes acceptance tests.

2025-02-26 17:20 - Marcus Lee: Security review of skip-webhook patch completed; no sensitive changes. Approving hotfix candidate for 3.2.1-hotfix1. Filing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1128

2025-02-27 02:05 - Customer Success (Priya Singh): Customer A accepted scheduled maintenance; we applied hotfix in their staging first then production within 4-hour window. Issue resolved for Customer A. Ongoing verification for Customer B/C.
2025-02-27 14:40 - QA (Liam O'Connor): Added e2e tests for CRD conversion edge cases and helm-hook timeouts. Tests added to pipeline and flake guard enabled.

2025-02-28 09:05 - Ava Chen: Deployed config-reconciliation job (cron: post-upgrade-validate-config) that compares live values against desired state and applies safe patches for known drift keys. Observed it fixed imagePullPolicy discrepancies in two clusters.

2025-02-28 13:00 - Marcus Lee: Preparing postmortem doc and customer communication template. Next steps: automated rollback in operator controller, telemetry alert for failed CRD conversion Webhook, schedule backfill to run reconciliation across Dedicated fleet.
next_steps: 1) Merge hotfix PR and cut release 3.2.1-hotfix1; 2) Promote automated rollback into operator controller (ENG-8910) with canary gating; 3) Expand reconciliation rules to cover all drifted keys; 4) Notify affected customers and update runbook; 5) Postmortem and follow-up action items assigned.
notes: Key trade-offs: skipping webhook conversion reduces upgrade strictness but risks leaving CRDs in older schema temporarily — mitigated by reconciliation job and follow-up CRD migration. Rollback automation must be conservative: only rollback on hook failures or operator crashloop for >5 mins to avoid unnecessary rollbacks.
